title: Defining the teeing area
question: When starting a hole, where must the ball be placed for your first shot from the teeing area?

choices.text: Anywhere within 2 club-lengths from the tee markers, even if your feet are outside.
Directly on the line joining the two tee markers.
Completely inside the teeing area, which is defined by the tee markers and up to two club-lengths behind them.
Anywhere on the teeing ground as long as your stance is inside it.

explanation: The ball must be entirely inside the teeing area for your first shot, although your stance can be outside the area.

juniorVersion.title: Where Can You Place Your Ball When Starting a Hole?
juniorVersion.question: When you start a hole, where should you put your ball on the tee to hit your first shot?

choices.text: Anywhere within 2 club-lengths of the tee markers, even if your feet stand outside.
Right between the two tee markers, in a straight line.
Completely inside the teeing area. This is between the two tee markers and up to two club-lengths behind them.
Anywhere on the tee, as long as your feet are inside the teeing area.

juniorVersion.explanation: Your ball has to be all the way inside the teeing area before you hit your first shot. Your feet can be outside, but your ball cannot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The markers show where the teeing area starts on each side.
The space where you start each hole. It is between the tee markers and goes back two club-lengths.
The length of your golf club. You can use it to measure the teeing area.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Set up two objects as tee markers and have kids practise placing the ball in the correct spot. Use a club to show how far back the teeing area goes.
likelyMisconceptions: That your feet must also be inside the teeing area when hitting.
That you have to put the ball right in line between the markers, not behind.
